tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Start with README.md to understand the project's purpose, features, and quick start guide. ARCHITECTURE.md then maps the functional areas, key execution flows, and design decisions that shape the codebase. Together they provide the roadmap for the tour ahead.

tour.title: Application Entry Point
tour.description: The main entry point bootstraps the Bubble Tea application, initializes the Viper config loader, slog logger, and all domain services, then starts the 5-tab TUI interface. This file gives a bird's-eye view of the runtime wiring.
tour.languageLesson: Go programs start at func main() in package main. This entry point wires up the Viper config loader, slog logger, domain services, and finally delegates to the Bubble Tea program loop.

tour.title: Configuration Bootstrap
tour.description: The Viper-based TOML loader provides path expansion, default values, and driver-specific defaults for the model-loader config. go.mod declares the Go 1.26.2 toolchain and Charmbracelet Bubble Tea dependencies that power the TUI.
tour.languageLesson: Go's mapstructure struct tags tell Viper how to map TOML keys to Go fields, enabling strongly typed configuration with automatic nested section support.

tour.title: Core Domain Models
tour.description: The type system defines Profile (the central persistence unit), BackendValidationSchema (presentation groups, cross-field rules, and schema source tracking), and FlagSchema (per-backend flag specifications). These structs establish the vocabulary used throughout the service layer.
tour.languageLesson: Go struct embedding lets BackendValidationSchema compose smaller structs into a single flat namespace, keeping the domain model declarative and extensible without deep nesting.

tour.title: Logging Infrastructure
tour.description: The logging package sets up session-based slog with file-only output, log rotation by session, and attempt ID generation. This keeps the terminal clean while preserving full traceability for debugging process launches and proxy traffic.
tour.languageLesson: Go's slog package provides structured logging with key-value pairs. Using a file-only handler with rotation avoids flooding the TUI terminal while preserving debuggability.

tour.title: Backend Catalog & Schema Management
tour.description: DefaultCatalog builds an in-memory catalog of llama.cpp backends with health probing. The schema manager orchestrates help parsing and generates validation schemas for each backend variant, including hand-curated fallback schemas.
tour.languageLesson: Go interfaces abstract persistence. Store and SchemaStore interfaces let the catalog swap filesystem storage for in-memory or remote implementations without changing business logic.

tour.title: Process Lifecycle Manager
tour.description: Manages llama-server process lifecycle including launch, health readiness, crash detection, and instance recovery from persistent state. The args builder converts profile configs into command-line flags for multiple backend kinds.
tour.languageLesson: Go goroutines run the background liveness probe independently of the TUI loop. Channels carry crash events and health state back to the manager, enabling concurrent process supervision without blocking the UI.

tour.title: Model Discovery & Scanning
tour.description: The model scanner orchestrates GGUF file discovery and extracts metadata including architecture, quantization format, and tensor info. This drives the Models tab and enables profile creation directly from downloaded files.
tour.languageLesson: Go's encoding/binary package handles GGUF's little-endian tensor headers. The scanner maps raw byte offsets to structured GGUFHeader and TensorInfo structs.

tour.title: HTTP Proxy Layer
tour.description: Provides an OpenAI-compatible reverse proxy for chat completions, translating OpenAI-shaped requests into llama-server endpoints. The proxy interface abstracts the contract so the TUI and benchmark engine can share the same HTTP surface.
tour.languageLesson: Go's http.Handler interface is the standard HTTP server contract. The proxy layer implements custom ServeHTTP methods to translate OpenAI-shaped requests into llama-server's native endpoints.

tour.title: Profile Persistence
tour.description: export.go bundles profiles into timestamped JSON with schema versioning for backup and sharing. history.go saves previous versions to a sidecar directory for undo support. Together they ensure profile data is durable and recoverable.
tour.languageLesson: Go's encoding/json with struct tags controls field naming and omitempty behavior. Atomic file writes via os.Rename after writing to a temp file prevent partial writes from corrupting profile state.

tour.title: TUI Root & Layout
tour.description: root.go implements the 5-tab Bubble Tea model with global shortcuts, help overlay, and message routing across pages. layout.go provides responsive panel sizing that adapts to terminal dimensions. confirm.go is the most reused component, consumed by eleven other files.
tour.languageLesson: Bubble Tea's Model-Update-View architecture mirrors React's state-reducer-render pattern in Go. Each page implements tea.Model with Init, Update, and View methods, and the root model dispatches tea.Msg values across the tab boundary.

tour.title: Build System & Schema Contract
tour.description: The Makefile defines build, install, and test targets. profile-schema.json is the authoritative JSON Schema for profile bundles, kept in strict sync with domain.Profile so persisted data never drifts from the code.
tour.languageLesson: Makefiles use phony targets for non-file actions like make build and make test. A JSON Schema document enforces contract validity independently of the Go type system, catching drift between code and persisted data.
